Replaces #38282, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted and recreated.

## Summary

- Capture logical expert IDs from DeepSeek V4 HashTopK before logical-to-physical remapping for R3 replay. Mask CUDA-graph padding, disable target capture from draft modules, and reject the unsupported HashTopK waterfill/capture combination.
- Synchronize CUDA IPC tensor imports in the weight updater before returning to the producer, including flattened buckets and other tensor load formats.
- Support repeated TRT-LLM MXFP4 online loads: permute expert weights in place, retain checkpoint-layout scale parameters, and maintain separate shuffled scale copies with stable kernel addresses. Pass unsigned byte views at the FlashInfer packed-FP4 call boundary without changing load parameters.
- Register the GEMM1 clamp limit as a non-persistent buffer so memory offload preserves it.
- Keep the padded-row Triton fast path off CPU tensors.

## Current rebase (2026-10-02)

Rebased the PR-only commits onto `sglang-miles` at `6c94e57f9ff5b84ba9746f5983ff13ce7e84c68b`. Current head: `0f0a367bad0d693ed8af044316111c25d919ed67`.

- `091bc49cf3`: restore the capture helper's original API, keep device checks at launch sites, validate routed MXFP4 hardware before model construction, and make the flattened-bucket helper's exception-only return contract explicit.
- `ec8a0fbf1c`: integrate upstream expert padding and input prequantization with hot reload. Recognize signed packed weights when computing hidden size and clear padding before repeat shuffles. Adapt existing tests to the current loader/runtime-context interfaces.

## Experiment terminology

- **P1:** TE MXFP8 training with MXFP8 rollout.
- **P2:** TE MXFP8 training with MXFP4 weights × MXFP8 activations for rollout routed experts, without trainer-side QAT.
- **P3:** The P2 setup with routed-expert MXFP4 fake quantization during training; trainer GEMMs still use TE MXFP8.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-02)

`0f0a367bad` adds inverse-shuffle restore for partial MXFP4 updates, live layer-buffer ownership for the clamp, XPU-compatible launch guards, in-place activation constant refresh, and first-build-only allocator cleanup. Empty/weight-only/scale-only sessions failed all six new cases before the restore fix and pass afterward.

The source stack also passed an ARM/GB300 preflight: 69 Miles integration tests, 6 QAT GPU tests and 30 SGLang tests (7 HashTopK, 9 MXFP4 GPU, 5 FP8 ownership, 9 UE8M0). Checkpoint metadata, optimizer/scheduler/RNG state and rollout data-state were audited before the pending P2 resume. This preflight is not an end-to-end training pass.

GitHub CI remains gated on `run-ci`. The PR author's attempt to add it was denied by GitHub permissions; a maintainer must add the label.

## Validation of the preceding rebase

- **320 CPU tests passed**, run one test file per process: HashTopK (7), model loader (3), derived-weight cache (2), FP8 runner fallback (4), runner ownership/static buffers (5), MegaMoE (6), routed capture (5), UE8M0 requantization (9), and server arguments (279).
- **3 B300 GPU tests passed**: fresh-load versus hot-reload parity and storage-address preservation for aligned/padded expert sizes, plus real MXFP4 x MXFP8 forward/reload with standard and FlashInfer dispatch inputs.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- No new end-to-end RL run was performed after this rebase. These local checks do not establish a full GitHub CI pass.

The results below are historical, from earlier heads.

## FP8/MXFP8 activation-state follow-up (2026-09-23)

Commit `104716dc91` also fixes the TRT-LLM activation tensors introduced in the new base's FP8/MXFP8 path. These alpha/beta/clamp tensors were ordinary attributes, so the memory-saver static-state backup omitted them. Repeated postprocessing also replaced their storage even though CUDA graphs retained the old addresses. Register them as non-persistent buffers and copy into existing storage on reload.

Evidence: an isolated reproduction using the actual preparation and static-state export/import functions left the old clamp at zero after simulated storage loss; re-preparation created a different pointer holding 10. The same function-level check passes after the fix (restored values, stable storage, no checkpoint entries). The existing runner-ownership test fixture now also covers this lifecycle.

The prior `23837cdabf` source passed 7 HashTopK tests and the GPU MXFP4 hot-reload test on GB300, but an end-to-end P1 run subsequently exhibited repetitive output and could not collect valid training groups. The activation-state defect is confirmed; attributing the complete rollout failure to it still requires a new RL run. Updated-source integration job completed successfully on GB300: 51 Miles integration tests, 6 GPU MXFP4 QAT tests, and 12 SGLang tests (HashTopK, MXFP4 hot reload, and FP8 runner ownership/activation-state lifecycle). Changed-file pre-commit passed with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`. P1 smoke, with all other source/config pins unchanged, collected valid normal-mode samples and completed one valid optimizer step (`ppo_kl=0`, rollout/train log-prob absolute difference 0.02877). It then failed with host-memory OOM during trainer CPU offload; this is not a three-step end-to-end pass. The first `actor_train` timer was 703.9 seconds, not a steady-state performance measurement. P1 retry subsequently **passed all three optimizer steps** and exited successfully (1:03:47), with the same source pins and training settings and additional host-memory diagnostics. `actor_train`: 699.8 / 127.0 / 105.5 seconds; `ppo_kl=0` for all three steps; train/rollout log-prob absolute difference 0.02852 / 0.02860 / 0.02731. No host or CUDA OOM was observed in this run. This does not establish the earlier host-OOM root cause: the physical nodes and Ray-head/PP-stage placement differed. P2 and P3 both failed during the initial SGLang autotune forward, before online weight sync or training: `ValueError: Unsupported trtllm-gen input tensor`. The MXFP4 method passed signed checkpoint parameters directly to FlashInfer instead of zero-copy unsigned-byte views; the same issue exists in the pre-rebase PR head. The idle outer launchers were cancelled. SGLang commit `f9cfbec2d2` fixes that boundary with zero-copy uint8 views, preserving signed load parameters and storage. The new real-kernel case fails with the original exception before the fix; after the fix, all 13 local B300 SGLang tests pass (including real MXFP4 x MXFP8 forward and reload). ARM preflight completed successfully: **70 tests passed** (51 Miles, 6 GPU QAT, 13 SGLang), exit `0:0`. P2 retry and P3 retry used `f9cfbec2d2` and subsequently failed at initial FP32 export quantization, as detailed below. The completed P1 run above used SGLang `104716dc91`; it predates this MXFP4-only follow-up.

P2 retry and P3 retry passed SGLang initialization but failed during initial online weight sync, before any optimizer step: the UE8M0 blockwise-FP8 helper rejected Bridge's FP32 export (`[2048, 4096]` shared-expert weight). This is separate from the preceding packed-MXFP4 kernel boundary bug.

SGLang commit `becddd92ece674066025b3e132768391b658214a` accepts BF16 or FP32 without changing the quantization math or rounding through BF16. Both new CPU regression cases fail before the fix. After it: 9 CPU tests and 13 related B300 GPU tests pass; the actual failing shape produces byte-identical FP8 weights and packed scales for BF16 weights versus their lossless FP32 exports. Changed-file pre-commit passes with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`.

ARM preflight completed (`0:0`, 4:35): **79 tests passed** (51 Miles, 6 GPU QAT, 22 SGLang).

### Completed direct-HF smoke, without Bridge #36

All three arms completed **three valid optimizer steps**, including repeated online weight updates and normal-mode rollout, and exited successfully. No host/CUDA OOM was observed in these successful runs; all nine logged `ppo_kl` values are zero, and loss/gradient norms are finite.

Pins: Miles P1 `946b00a41c`, P2/P3 `f7c4529350`; unmodified Bridge `bridge` base `2e09c234a`; Megatron-LM `f2fc0efcb`. P1 used SGLang `104716dc91`; P2/P3 used `becddd92ec`, which adds the packed-MXFP4 boundary fix and FP32 UE8M0 input support. **P1 was not rerun at the final SGLang head.** All code was committed source; no runtime/site-packages patches or offline weight conversion.

LGTM — nice set of fixes, and the comments explaining *why* each invariant exists make this much easier to review than it could have been.

Things I checked independently and that hold up:

- The shuffle refactor is equivalent against FlashInfer 0.6.18: `shuffle_matrix_a(x, t) == x[get_shuffle_matrix_a_row_indices(x, t)]` and `shuffle_matrix_sf_a(x, t) == block_scale_interleave(x[get_shuffle_matrix_sf_a_row_indices(x, t)])`, with `num_elts_per_sf` defaulting to 16. Folding `[w1, w3] -> [w3, w1]` into the gather as `w3_w1_rows[perm[r]]` reproduces the old `shuffle(reorder(w))` ordering, and `half` is valid for the scales too since their row count matches `w13.shape[1]`.
- `supports_output_view` is a real per-backend attribute in `flashinfer/moe_ep` (`modes/mega_layer.py` plus the cutedsl backends), so gating on it is a genuine fix rather than a guess — the DeepGEMM mega path doesn't advertise it.
- `get_platform().is_sm100` resolves to `device_capability_majors=[10]`, so sm_103 (B300/GB300) passes. Good, given where this was validated.
- Every call site of the new `capture_routed_experts_if_allowed(allow_capture, ...)` signature is updated, and `HashTopK` is a plain `nn.Module`, so the `isinstance` chain in `disable_routed_experts_capture_for_draft` is safe.
- Merges cleanly onto current `sglang-miles` (only `topk.py` overlaps the 12 commits since the base).

A few comments, none blocking.

## 1. `Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod` has no `restore_weights_before_loading`

This is the one I'd most like addressed. `process_weights_after_loading` now permutes `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` in place, which makes it non-idempotent. `restore_weight` in `model_loader/loader.py` is the hook for exactly this ("Undo in-place quant packing so fresh weights can be loaded"), and `Mxfp4MoEMethod.restore_weights_before_loading` implements it for the Marlin path.

Without it, `begin_weight_update` -> a session that updates only non-MoE tensors -> `end_weight_update` runs `postprocess_weight` over already-permuted weights and permutes them a second time, silently. A full-model sync is unaffected, so this doesn't touch the validated recipe — but `/begin_weight_update` and `/update_weights_from_tensor` are public endpoints and the name list is caller-controlled. Applying the inverse permutation (`argsort(w13_rows)` / `argsort(w2_rows)`) in a restore hook would make the postprocess correct either way.

Related, in `test_mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_hot_reload.py`: the `restore_weight(layer, torch.device("cuda"))` call and the assertions after it are currently a no-op, since `_apply_quant_method_hook` does a `hasattr` check and skips the method. So the "loader hooks bracket every update session; neither may disturb the checkpoint-layout parameters" half of that test isn't actually exercised yet.

## 2. The `*_shuffled` split has two consequences worth a comment

- **Memory**: the fp32 checkpoint-layout scales used to be freed when they were replaced by the shuffled version. Now both layouts stay resident; the fp32 copy alone is roughly a quarter the size of `w13_weight`. Necessary for reloadability, just worth stating.
- **EPLB**: `DeepseekV2MoE.get_moe_weights` picks up `w13_weight_scale_inv_shuffled` only because `copy_or_rebind_param` registers it as a `Parameter` and `filter_moe_weight_param_global_expert` admits anything with `shape[0] == num_local_experts`. That's load-bearing — if these ever became buffers, a rebalance would update the checkpoint-layout scales and leave the kernel reading stale shuffled ones. A one-line comment pinning that would help.

## 3. `apply()` reads the method attribute, not the buffer

`gemm1_clamp_limit=self._gemm1_clamp_limit_tensor` — but the reason for `register_buffer` is that the *layer's* copy is what offload maintains. They agree today because `_import_static_state` restores in place, but `nn.Module._apply` (`.to()`, `.cuda()`) replaces `_buffers[key]` outright and would strand the method's reference. Reading `layer._gemm1_clamp_limit_tensor` matches what the FP8 side already does.

## 4. `_can_fuse_padded_region`: `x.is_cuda` also excludes XPU

On XPU both `_is_cuda` and `_is_npu` are False, so a tensor reaches this predicate and now falls back to eager even though Triton works there. The comment says "fall back to eager for host tensors"; `not x.is_cpu` matches that intent exactly and keeps ROCm and XPU on the fused path.

## 5. Smaller things

- `get_quant_method`: after the SM100 raise, the `is_sm90 or is_sm120` branch is unreachable for `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`, so the comment above it now describes only the `flashinfer_mxfp4` arm. One check placed just before the TRT-LLM return would cover both backends and remove the dead branch — at the cost of changing `flashinfer_mxfp4` behaviour on unsupported arches, which may be a separate decision.
- `apply()`: `w13` / `w2` are now unconditionally uint8 views, so `... if w2.dtype == torch.uint8 else ...` can't take the `else`.
- `_update_weights_from_flattened_bucket`'s `return True, "Success"` is now discarded by the caller.
- `_prepare_flashinfer_trtllm_activation_params`: `existing.fill_(float(value))` would skip building `tensor` on the reload path. Also `existing is not None and tensor is None` falls into the `register_buffer` branch, which is the pointer-orphaning case the in-place branch exists to prevent — unreachable while `moe_runner_config` is fixed for the layer's lifetime, but the condition reads as though it were handled.
- `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` at the end of `process_weights_after_loading` now runs per MoE layer on every weight-update session. With the in-place design there's far less to reclaim than before, so it may be worth restricting to the first build.
- `disable_routed_experts_capture_for_draft`: `elif hasattr(module, "allow_routed_experts_capture")` would cover `HashTopK` and any future router class without the lazy import and without another `elif` next time.
- `HashTopK.allow_routed_experts_capture` could be a class attribute next to the docstring with the same "draft-side blocks set this False" comment that `TopKConfig` carries; right now the HashTopK side has no explanation of what the flag is for.

## 6. CI hasn't run on this head

All the check failures are the same gate — `Missing required label 'run-ci'` — and every suite is `skipping`. Worth adding the label so the six new test files actually execute before this lands.

Addressed in 091bc49cf3. Restored `capture_routed_experts_if_allowed` and its existing callers to the original `TopKConfig` API. HashTopK now owns a `TopKConfig` too, so target/draft capture uses the same opt-out flag without changing the helper. The 7 HashTopK tests pass.

Addressed in 091bc49cf3. `_can_fuse_padded_region` is unchanged from the base again; the device check now lives at the two launch call sites. The predicate remains layout-only, and ROCm tensors still satisfy PyTorch's `is_cuda` check.

> 🤖 **Posted autonomously by Claude Code acting on the user's behalf.** Single-pass diff review of this PR; one correctness concern found. Please push back if the conclusion is off.

**`update_weights_from_tensor` now ignores the `flattened_bucket` helper's return value.**

Before this PR, the `flattened_bucket` branch returned the result of `_update_weights_from_flattened_bucket(...)` directly. After the refactor, that call's return value is discarded and the function falls through to the unconditional `return True, "Success"`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/d6d709637bf12c95377c200b3a3fb9fe40736102/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/weight_updater.py#L571-L588

**Severity note (verified against the head source):** today `_update_weights_from_flattened_bucket` can only fail by raising — its sole return is `(True, "Success")` ([weight_updater.py#L423-L453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/d6d709637bf12c95377c200b3a3fb9fe40736102/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/weight_updater.py#L423-L453)) — so there is no live behavior change. It is a latent trap: if that helper ever starts reporting failure via its return tuple, the caller will silently report success. Suggest either propagating the status or changing the helper to return `None` so the convention is explicit.

@Zhichenzzz Addressed the flattened-bucket return-value finding in 091bc49cf3: the internal helper now explicitly returns `None` and raises on reconstruction/load failure. The public method still synchronizes the device before returning `(True, "Success")`, so no helper status is silently discarded and CUDA IPC lifetime protection is preserved.

@HJSang Follow-up to your review: addressed in 0f0a367bad.

1. The TRT-LLM MXFP4 method now implements the `QuantizeMethodBase` restore contract. It inverse-permutes weights in place before updates, preserving parameter/storage identity; repeated restore/postprocess calls are safe. Empty, weight-only and scale-only update sessions failed all 6 regression cases before the fix and pass afterward, with both padded and aligned dimensions.
2. Documented the retained FP32 scales' memory cost and why shuffled scales must remain Parameters for EPLB.
3. `apply()` reads the layer's live clamp buffer. The real-kernel test now replaces buffers through `Module._apply` and invalidates the old clamp reference.
4. Launch sites use `not tensor.is_cpu`, preserving the XPU/ROCm fused path. XPU execution was not tested locally.
5. Removed the dead uint8 conditional, made activation-buffer reload use `fill_` and reject enabled/disabled transitions, and limited `empty_cache()` to the first layout build. The flattened helper's `None` return was fixed in 091bc49cf3. HashTopK now shares `TopKConfig`, so its flag documentation and draft opt-out follow the existing contract rather than a new duck-typed attribute. The earlier model-load validation keeps the existing `flashinfer_mxfp4` architecture support unchanged.
6. I tried adding `run-ci`, but GitHub rejected it with `AddLabelsToLabelable` permission denied. Could a maintainer please add the label?

reviews.body:
LGTM — nice set of fixes, and the comments explaining *why* each invariant exists make this much easier to review than it could have been.

Things I checked independently and that hold up:

- The shuffle refactor is equivalent against FlashInfer 0.6.18: `shuffle_matrix_a(x, t) == x[get_shuffle_matrix_a_row_indices(x, t)]` and `shuffle_matrix_sf_a(x, t) == block_scale_interleave(x[get_shuffle_matrix_sf_a_row_indices(x, t)])`, with `num_elts_per_sf` defaulting to 16. Folding `[w1, w3] -> [w3, w1]` into the gather as `w3_w1_rows[perm[r]]` reproduces the old `shuffle(reorder(w))` ordering, and `half` is valid for the scales too since their row count matches `w13.shape[1]`.
- `supports_output_view` is a real per-backend attribute in `flashinfer/moe_ep` (`modes/mega_layer.py` plus the cutedsl backends), so gating on it is a genuine fix rather than a guess — the DeepGEMM mega path doesn't advertise it.
- `get_platform().is_sm100` resolves to `device_capability_majors=[10]`, so sm_103 (B300/GB300) passes. Good, given where this was validated.
- Every call site of the new `capture_routed_experts_if_allowed(allow_capture, ...)` signature is updated, and `HashTopK` is a plain `nn.Module`, so the `isinstance` chain in `disable_routed_experts_capture_for_draft` is safe.
- Merges cleanly onto current `sglang-miles` (only `topk.py` overlaps the 12 commits since the base).

A few comments, none blocking.

## 1. `Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod` has no `restore_weights_before_loading`

This is the one I'd most like addressed. `process_weights_after_loading` now permutes `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` in place, which makes it non-idempotent. `restore_weight` in `model_loader/loader.py` is the hook for exactly this ("Undo in-place quant packing so fresh weights can be loaded"), and `Mxfp4MoEMethod.restore_weights_before_loading` implements it for the Marlin path.

Without it, `begin_weight_update` -> a session that updates only non-MoE tensors -> `end_weight_update` runs `postprocess_weight` over already-permuted weights and permutes them a second time, silently. A full-model sync is unaffected, so this doesn't touch the validated recipe — but `/begin_weight_update` and `/update_weights_from_tensor` are public endpoints and the name list is caller-controlled. Applying the inverse permutation (`argsort(w13_rows)` / `argsort(w2_rows)`) in a restore hook would make the postprocess correct either way.

Related, in `test_mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_hot_reload.py`: the `restore_weight(layer, torch.device("cuda"))` call and the assertions after it are currently a no-op, since `_apply_quant_method_hook` does a `hasattr` check and skips the method. So the "loader hooks bracket every update session; neither may disturb the checkpoint-layout parameters" half of that test isn't actually exercised yet.

## 2. The `*_shuffled` split has two consequences worth a comment

- **Memory**: the fp32 checkpoint-layout scales used to be freed when they were replaced by the shuffled version. Now both layouts stay resident; the fp32 copy alone is roughly a quarter the size of `w13_weight`. Necessary for reloadability, just worth stating.
- **EPLB**: `DeepseekV2MoE.get_moe_weights` picks up `w13_weight_scale_inv_shuffled` only because `copy_or_rebind_param` registers it as a `Parameter` and `filter_moe_weight_param_global_expert` admits anything with `shape[0] == num_local_experts`. That's load-bearing — if these ever became buffers, a rebalance would update the checkpoint-layout scales and leave the kernel reading stale shuffled ones. A one-line comment pinning that would help.

## 3. `apply()` reads the method attribute, not the buffer

`gemm1_clamp_limit=self._gemm1_clamp_limit_tensor` — but the reason for `register_buffer` is that the *layer's* copy is what offload maintains. They agree today because `_import_static_state` restores in place, but `nn.Module._apply` (`.to()`, `.cuda()`) replaces `_buffers[key]` outright and would strand the method's reference. Reading `layer._gemm1_clamp_limit_tensor` matches what the FP8 side already does.

## 4. `_can_fuse_padded_region`: `x.is_cuda` also excludes XPU

On XPU both `_is_cuda` and `_is_npu` are False, so a tensor reaches this predicate and now falls back to eager even though Triton works there. The comment says "fall back to eager for host tensors"; `not x.is_cpu` matches that intent exactly and keeps ROCm and XPU on the fused path.

## 5. Smaller things

- `get_quant_method`: after the SM100 raise, the `is_sm90 or is_sm120` branch is unreachable for `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`, so the comment above it now describes only the `flashinfer_mxfp4` arm. One check placed just before the TRT-LLM return would cover both backends and remove the dead branch — at the cost of changing `flashinfer_mxfp4` behaviour on unsupported arches, which may be a separate decision.
- `apply()`: `w13` / `w2` are now unconditionally uint8 views, so `... if w2.dtype == torch.uint8 else ...` can't take the `else`.
- `_update_weights_from_flattened_bucket`'s `return True, "Success"` is now discarded by the caller.
- `_prepare_flashinfer_trtllm_activation_params`: `existing.fill_(float(value))` would skip building `tensor` on the reload path. Also `existing is not None and tensor is None` falls into the `register_buffer` branch, which is the pointer-orphaning case the in-place branch exists to prevent — unreachable while `moe_runner_config` is fixed for the layer's lifetime, but the condition reads as though it were handled.
- `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` at the end of `process_weights_after_loading` now runs per MoE layer on every weight-update session. With the in-place design there's far less to reclaim than before, so it may be worth restricting to the first build.
- `disable_routed_experts_capture_for_draft`: `elif hasattr(module, "allow_routed_experts_capture")` would cover `HashTopK` and any future router class without the lazy import and without another `elif` next time.
- `HashTopK.allow_routed_experts_capture` could be a class attribute next to the docstring with the same "draft-side blocks set this False" comment that `TopKConfig` carries; right now the HashTopK side has no explanation of what the flag is for.

## 6. CI hasn't run on this head

All the check failures are the same gate — `Missing required label 'run-ci'` — and every suite is `skipping`. Worth adding the label so the six new test files actually execute before this lands.
